title: Extend the rank dual to four planes: COPY floor 16 over every field on 361,706 of 367,290 plane quadruples; 5,584 open (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

This adds `research/four-plane-rank-dual/`. It extends the rank-dual line from CubeJerry's #4365 (two planes) and my #4421 (three planes, all 27,720 triples) to **four-plane decoders**, under #4365's contract unchanged.

**Claim type:** exact all-field lower-bound certificates, checked in stdlib, plus an explicitly open remainder. **No new κ.**

## Result

- **361,706 of 367,290 plane quadruples (98.48%) have four-plane COPY floor 16 = Σ p_i² over every field.** That equals separate coordinate messages, so four-plane mixing cannot lower the COPY mass on them.
- **Certificates.** `L(M) = Σ_{(Z,X)} w·rank(Φ_Z(M)_XX)`, where `Φ_Z` zeroes off-diagonal plane blocks. Atom ranks are bounded combinatorially, over every field. There are 9,330 distinct certificates, all of value 16:
  - block-rank certificates cover 195,523 classes;
  - zeroed-block and mixed certificates cover 24,732 more.
- **Open: 5,584 quadruples in 3,650 classes.** Their best LP over all 4,096 × 15 zero-set and union pairs ranges from 12.571 to just under 16. They typically pair a free plane pair (cross rank 0) with a cheap full closure (joint Gram rank 5–7). The fractional covering relies on uncancelled free cross atoms, as in the triples. These are **undecided, not counterexamples**: an exact `F₂` ILP (65,025 atoms, mass ≤ 15) and a short real-coefficient search on one class were both inconclusive.

## Evidence

```text
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/four-plane-rank-dual --check-only
  PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/four-plane-rank-dual
  PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/four-plane-rank-dual outcome=completed   (~4.5 min, stdlib only)
```

`verify.py` recomputes all 367,290 quadruples' tariffs from the pinned archive and matching and builds its own bound table. It then checks each referenced certificate exactly, with integer-scaled weights. The artifacts are small: `CERTIFICATES.json.gz` (91 KB) and `CERT-INDEX.bin.gz` (384 KB). `generation/` documents the scipy scripts that produced them.

Head: `ea69e19eec31e8b2b93c4e41fa2d0c0d6c6da4ab`. Base: canonical main `2a13eb18`, the selected-#4359 refresh.

## Not covered

- The ℚ/ℂ minimum on the open quadruples.
- Five or more planes.
- Native realization and coverage.

- **Claim:** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19108055
